anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer selects or reuses a highly sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are reasonably accurate.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly: Obsolete row versions and rollback records accumulate faster than background cleaners can reclaim them, inflating the live data set.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Free space for data files, logs, temp areas, or archives is exhausted or about to hit hard limits.

Composite Definition
This composite anomaly describes a condition in which the database simultaneously suffers from (1) poor execution-plan choices, (2) runaway accumulation of MVCC garbage, and (3) dwindling physical or logical storage space. The workload therefore experiences the combined pressure of inefficient query execution, table and index bloat, and imminent space exhaustion.

Combined Observable Phenomena
• Queries that suddenly switch from index access to full or bitmap scans, run far longer than usual, and generate large temporary-space spills.
• Rapid growth of base tables, indexes, undo/rollback segments, and transaction logs; version-store or vacuum/cleaner processes remain perpetually backlogged.
• Free space graphs show step-function drops; auto-extend/auto-grow requests fail or pause; warning messages cite both "no space left" and "vacuum not keeping up" conditions.
• Statistics drift because bloated pages distort row counts, causing even more unstable plan flips and further execution-time variance.
• End-user symptoms include sporadic timeouts, "cannot allocate space" errors, and unpredictable throughput collapse during peak update or reporting windows.

Causal Chain and Reinforcement Mechanisms
1. Sub-optimal plans (e.g., full table scans or poorly parallelized nested loops) read and modify far more pages than necessary, inflating undo/redo and version chains.
2. The enlarged version store slows visibility checks, prolonging transaction lifetimes; long-running or stalled queries hold old snapshots, preventing cleanup workers from reclaiming dead rows.
3. As MVCC garbage accumulates, table and index bloat consume additional disk space, forcing the storage subsystem toward its capacity limits.
4. Approaching space limits throttle or fail further writes, which in turn can invalidate cached plans, trigger plan recompilations, or disable adaptive features—raising the likelihood of yet more sub-optimal plan choices.
5. The feedback loop—bad plans → more version churn → storage bloat → space pressure → plan instability—amplifies latency and risk of outright service interruption, making the composite failure harder to diagnose than any single anomaly in isolation.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
